scenes.line1: How do APIs prevent duplicate POSTs?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how APIs avoid duplicate POST requests and stay reliable?

scenes.label: Idempotency
scenes.sub: A unique key lets clients retry safely.
scenes.say: Idempotency keys are unique values. They let clients retry POSTs without creating duplicates.

scenes.title: POST /payments
scenes.say: For example, a payment API uses an idempotency key in the request header.
APIs handle retries, enforce rate limits with status four-two-nine, and document their limits clearly.

scenes.question: What happens if you skip idempotency?
scenes.right: Skipping idempotency risks duplicate resources on retries.
scenes.say: Interview trap: If you skip idempotency, clients may create duplicates when retrying POST requests.
